leads.description: A signer or validator load balancer is internet-facing and has a listener. Backend reachability and authentication are not tested. Fix: keep the signing endpoint private.
A ConfigMap stores an EVM private key in plain text. ConfigMaps are not a secret store. No balance or live use is checked. Fix: use an isolated signing service and rotate the exposed key.

A Service selects a signer workload and uses NodePort. NodePort alone does not prove internet routing. A public LoadBalancer requests external exposure. Fix: use a private ClusterIP service and restrict ingress.

A public LoadBalancer maps to an RPC listener on all interfaces with admin, debug, or personal namespaces enabled. This is a configured path, not a live RPC test. Fix: remove administrative namespaces from public RPC.

A CI service account is bound to a role that can create pods/exec requests in a namespace containing a signer. This is declared RBAC access, not proof that a token was stolen. Fix: remove exec permission and separate deploy access from signing workloads.

A key-policy Allow gives the wildcard principal kms:Sign without a restricting condition. The key can authorize signing. This does not prove a deployed key or a usable transaction signature. Fix: restrict the principal and signing conditions.

A public-address signer instance references a security group with world ingress. This declares network exposure, not a deployed route or a successful signing request. Fix: remove public ingress and use a private signer network.

The front-end bucket requests a public-write ACL without a blocking public-ACL configuration. An applied policy can let strangers replace front-end assets. Fix: remove public-write and enable public-access blocks.

An assumable role trusts every principal and can read objects in every bucket. Any holder of the assumed credential reads data outside its own workload. The pinned source alone does not show the read. The live moto replay assumes the role and reads an unrelated bucket. Fix: limit the trust, the actions and the bucket pattern.

findings.title: hot-wallet-key-in-config
findings.explanation: A ConfigMap stores an EVM private key in plain text. ConfigMaps are not a secret store. No balance or live use is checked. Fix: use an isolated signing service and rotate the exposed key.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: broad-kms-sign
findings.explanation: A key-policy Allow gives the wildcard principal kms:Sign without a restricting condition. The key can authorize signing. This does not prove a deployed key or a usable transaction signature. Fix: restrict the principal and signing conditions.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: internet-rpc-admin-namespaces
findings.explanation: A public LoadBalancer maps to an RPC listener on all interfaces with admin, debug, or personal namespaces enabled. This is a configured path, not a live RPC test. Fix: remove administrative namespaces from public RPC.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: public-signer-load-balancer
findings.explanation: A signer or validator load balancer is internet-facing and has a listener. Backend reachability and authentication are not tested. Fix: keep the signing endpoint private.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: exposed-signer-service
findings.explanation: A Service selects a signer workload and uses NodePort. NodePort alone does not prove internet routing. A public LoadBalancer requests external exposure. Fix: use a private ClusterIP service and restrict ingress.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: internet-signer-security-group
findings.explanation: A public-address signer instance references a security group with world ingress. This declares network exposure, not a deployed route or a successful signing request. Fix: remove public ingress and use a private signer network.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: ci-can-exec-signers
findings.explanation: A CI service account is bound to a role that can create pods/exec requests in a namespace containing a signer. This is declared RBAC access, not proof that a token was stolen. Fix: remove exec permission and separate deploy access from signing workloads.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.

findings.title: frontend-public-write
findings.explanation: The front-end bucket requests a public-write ACL without a blocking public-ACL configuration. An applied policy can let strangers replace front-end assets. Fix: remove public-write and enable public-access blocks.

proof.detail: Allowlisted detector confirmed the pinned evidence.
